rows.text: Valgavoth draws you a card and grows whenever an opponent loses life for the first time during THEIR OWN turn — once per opponent, per turn cycle. That is the design constraint the whole deck answers: every punisher here is a passive that fires on somebody else's turn. Play a land, take two. Cast a spell, take two. Draw a card, take one. Each of those is a card for you and a counter on a flier that quickly gets out of reach.

rows.name: Valgavoth, Harrower of Souls
rows.text: 4/4 flier with ward—pay 2 life, and a +1/+1 counter plus a CARD every time an opponent loses life for the first time on their own turn. In a four-player pod that is three cards a round.
The trigger is once per opponent per turn, and only on their turn. Damage you deal on your own turn does nothing for it — so the punishers below are not just a clock, they are the draw engine.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste and shroud, because a ward of two life stops almost nothing.

rows.name: Mithril Coat
rows.text: flash, indestructible, attaches itself. Hold it as a counterspell for removal.

guide.title: Punishers that fire on their turn

rows.name: Polluted Bonds
rows.text: two life every time an opponent plays a land. It triggers on the first land drop of their turn, every turn, from every opponent. This is the best Valgavoth enabler in the deck.

rows.name: Roiling Vortex
rows.text: a point at each player's upkeep — guaranteed, from every opponent, before they do anything — plus five damage to anyone casting something for free.

rows.name: Spellshock
rows.text: two damage per spell, from every player.

rows.name: Pyrostatic Pillar
rows.text: two damage on every cheap spell, which is most of what a table casts.

rows.name: The Frightful Four
rows.text: their first noncreature spell each turn costs its mana value in life.

rows.name: Gleeful Arsonist
rows.text: damage equal to its power on every noncreature spell they cast, and undying brings it back bigger.

rows.name: Harsh Mentor
rows.text: two damage for every nonmana activated ability they use.

rows.name: Fate Unraveler
rows.text: a damage per card they draw — including their draw step.

rows.name: Razorkin Needlehead
rows.text: the same, and it first-strikes on your turn.

rows.name: Kederekt Parasite
rows.text: another copy while you control a red permanent.

rows.name: Scrawling Crawler
rows.text: forces everyone to draw at your upkeep and taxes every draw they take.

rows.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
rows.text: two life per card they draw, and two GAINED per card you draw.

rows.name: Blood Seeker
rows.text: a life for every creature they play.

rows.name: Tunnel Ignus
rows.text: three damage for every extra land a ramp deck plays in a turn.

rows.name: Revenge of Ravens
rows.text: attacking you costs a life per creature and gains you one.

rows.name: Exquisite Blood
rows.text: whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much.

rows.name: Enduring Tenacity
rows.text: whenever you gain life, an opponent loses that much.
The two together feed each other until the table is dead. It is two cards and needs no combat: allowed in Bracket 3, used from turn 6 on.

rows.name: Bloodthirsty Conqueror
rows.text: the second copy of the Exquisite Blood half, on a 5/5 flying deathtoucher.

rows.name: Bloodchief Ascension
rows.text: three quest counters comes fast when the table is losing life every turn, and then every card into any opponent's graveyard drains two more.

rows.name: Solphim, Mayhem Dominus
rows.text: doubles all noncombat damage you deal to opponents. Every punisher above fires twice as hard.

rows.name: Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might
rows.text: any red source you control dealing noncombat damage below its power deals FOUR instead. Pyrostatic Pillar's two becomes four; Fate Unraveler's one becomes four.

cards.name: Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might // Temple of Power

rows.name: Lasting Tarfire
rows.text: two damage to each opponent at every end step you put a counter on a creature — and Valgavoth puts counters on himself constantly.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: deathtouch and lifelink on a pinger turns every ping into a dead creature and a life gain, which Enduring Tenacity converts straight back into their life loss.

rows.name: Chandra's Ignition
rows.text: point it at Valgavoth once he has grown. His power hits every other creature on the board and every opponent in the face.

rows.name: Crawlspace
rows.text: no more than two creatures can attack you each combat.

rows.name: Silent Arbiter
rows.text: no more than one attacks, and no more than one blocks.

rows.name: Koskun Falls
rows.text: tap a creature at upkeep and they need three creatures to attack you at all.

rows.name: No Mercy
rows.text: anything that damages you dies.

rows.name: Forcefield
rows.text: reduces the one big attacker that does get through to a single point.

rows.name: Revenge of Ravens
rows.text: attacking you is a losing proposition even before the above.

rows.name: Kardur, Doomscourge
rows.text: forces their board to attack each other instead of you, and drains for every creature that dies.

rows.name: Ophiomancer
rows.text: a deathtouch Snake every upkeep, which blocks anything.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it redirects the removal aimed at Valgavoth.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: a scalable wrath your enchantments ignore.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: cheap, and this deck's threats are mostly enchantments.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: Rakdos's only clean answer to an enchantment or planeswalker.

rows.name: Rakdos Charm
rows.text: graveyard hate, an artifact, or a symmetric ping that finishes a token board.

rows.name: Shadowspear
rows.text: strips hexproof and indestructible, and gives Valgavoth trample and lifelink.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your creatures get ward.

rows.name: Liquimetal Torque
rows.text: fixes, and turns a problem permanent into an artifact you can destroy.

rows.name: Jeska's Will
rows.text: with a commander out, both halves.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, paid in life you are gaining back.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card — usually Polluted Bonds or a combo half.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana for the best creature in any graveyard.

rows.name: The One Ring
rows.text: a turn of protection and then an escalating draw engine.

rows.name: The Soul Stone
rows.text: once harnessed, a creature back every upkeep.

rows.name: Boggart Trawler
rows.text: graveyard hate on a body, or a land when you need one.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a rock and a cheap punisher. Pyrostatic Pillar or Roiling Vortex on turn two means Valgavoth is drawing you three cards a round from the moment he lands.

Prioritise the punishers that trigger on THEIR turn over the ones that trigger on yours. Polluted Bonds and Roiling Vortex are worth more here than any amount of damage you can deal in your own main phase.

rows.name: Valgavoth, Harrower of Souls
rows.text: four mana and a flier, so he is safe to deploy on curve. He is also the deck's card advantage — losing him costs you three cards a turn, so hold Mithril Coat or Deflecting Swat when you can.

Watch your own life total. Roiling Vortex and Spellshock hit you too, and Black Market Connections, Toxic Deluge and Reanimate all cost life. Enduring Tenacity and Bloodthirsty Conqueror are what make that sustainable — get one down before you start spending.
